_comment: GRAND over the FULL Arequipa DEM (10204 x 12603 px, ~129 Mpx), as opposed to the Colca crop in grand_colca_config.json. Same dem_path, origin and downsample_factor as the other arequipa_full config so the two masks are pixel-aligned and combinable. Every other criterion is unchanged from the crop config, deliberately: the point of this run is scale, not a different question.
_comment_downsample: 4, not 1. The estimator puts this DEM at 7.2 GiB of anonymous memory at 1 and 5.1 GiB at 4, against ~6-7 GiB typically free; the run measured 5.68 GiB peak RSS. Downsampling is the weaker of the two memory levers -- it scales the labelling arrays as its inverse square but not the candidates, which are taken on the native grid -- so pass --max-memory-gb rather than expecting a higher factor to rescue a small machine. Note the cost: area is measured on the downsampled mask while capacity is measured at full resolution, so a feature a few pixels wide loses area while keeping its detectors. That matters more for TAMBO's canyon strips than for GRAND's blobs, and it is the reason the crop configs use 1. Read areas from these runs as lower bounds.
_comment_origin: Deliberately null: read from the DEM's own ModelTiepointTag. The crop configs carry the crop's corner, which is not this file's.
